title: Current and circuits
summary: Charge, current, potential difference and resistance, resistivity, Ohm’s law and I–V characteristics, power, series and parallel circuits, potential dividers and internal resistance.

keyterms.definition: Rate of flow of charge, I = Δq/Δt, measured in amperes.
Work done per unit charge moving between two points, V = W/q, measured in volts.
Ratio of potential difference to current, R = V/I, measured in ohms.
For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature, current is proportional to potential difference.
Material property ρ in R = ρL/A, measured in Ω m.
Energy transferred to each coulomb of charge by a source, ε = W/q.
Resistance inside a source, causing lost volts: ε = I(R + r).
Resistors in series used to provide a fraction of a supply voltage.
A component whose resistance decreases as light intensity increases.
A component whose resistance decreases as temperature increases.
Average speed of charge carriers along a conductor, from I = nAvq.

questions.text: A current of 0.50 A flows for 2.0 minutes. The charge that passes is ___ C.

questions.prompt: A 12 V supply drives 0.40 A through a resistor. What is its resistance?

questions.statement: A filament lamp is an ohmic conductor.
questions.explanation: As the filament heats up its resistance increases, so its I–V graph curves and current is not proportional to p.d.

questions.prompt: A wire is replaced by one of the same material with twice the length and twice the cross-sectional area. Its resistance
questions.explanation: R = ρL/A: doubling L doubles R, doubling A halves it, so R is unchanged.

questions.text: A 2.0 kW kettle runs on a 230 V supply. The current it draws is about ___ A.

questions.prompt: Match each equation to its use.
questions.explanation: Choose the power equation that uses the quantities you know.

questions.prompt: A resistor dissipates 4.0 W when the current is 1.0 A. What power is dissipated when the current is 2.0 A?
questions.explanation: P = I²R, so doubling I quadruples P: 16 W.

questions.statement: The drift speed of electrons in a typical copper wire is less than 1 mm s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Copper has a huge density of free electrons, so I = nAvq gives a tiny v for ordinary currents.

questions.prompt: As the temperature of an NTC thermistor rises, its resistance
questions.explanation: More charge carriers are released at higher temperature, so the resistance falls.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to determine the resistivity of a wire experimentally.
items: Measure the wire’s diameter with a micrometer
Measure R for several lengths L
Plot R against L and find the gradient
Multiply the gradient by the cross-sectional area
questions.explanation: Gradient = ρ/A, so ρ = gradient × A; using several lengths reduces random error.

lessons.title: Circuits, potential dividers and internal resistance

questions.prompt: What is the total resistance of 6.0 Ω and 3.0 Ω connected in parallel?
questions.explanation: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2.0 Ω, less than the smallest resistor.

questions.text: Resistors of 4.0 Ω and 8.0 Ω are in series across 12 V. The p.d. across the 8.0 Ω resistor is ___ V.
questions.explanation: Current = 12/12 = 1.0 A, so V = 1.0 × 8.0 = 8.0 V: the p.d. divides in proportion to resistance.

questions.statement: In a series circuit the current is the same through every component.
questions.explanation: Charge is conserved and there is only one path, so the current is the same everywhere.

questions.prompt: A cell of e.m.f. 6.0 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω is connected to a 5.0 Ω resistor. What is the terminal p.d.?
questions.explanation: I = ε/(R + r) = 6.0/6.0 = 1.0 A; terminal p.d. = IR = 5.0 V (1.0 V is lost inside the cell).

questions.prompt: In a potential divider an LDR is the lower resistor, with the output taken across it. When light intensity increases, the output voltage
questions.explanation: The LDR’s resistance falls, so it takes a smaller share of the supply voltage.

questions.prompt: Match each item to its description.

pairs.right: Current into a junction equals current out
Sum of e.m.f.s equals sum of p.d.s in a loop

questions.explanation: Kirchhoff’s laws express conservation of charge and of energy.

questions.text: The difference between a cell’s e.m.f. and its terminal p.d. is called the ___ volts.
questions.explanation: Lost volts = Ir, the energy per coulomb dissipated in the internal resistance.

questions.statement: Adding another resistor in parallel to a circuit increases the total resistance.
questions.explanation: An extra parallel path lets more current flow, so the total resistance decreases.

questions.prompt: A graph of terminal p.d. (y) against current (x) for a cell is a straight line. What are its y-intercept and gradient?
questions.explanation: V = ε − Ir, so the intercept is the e.m.f. and the gradient is −r.

questions.prompt: Three identical 6.0 Ω resistors: two in parallel, then in series with the third. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: Parallel pair = 3.0 Ω; plus 6.0 Ω in series gives 9.0 Ω.
